content:
maya: heads-up — new intake from sales for a 13B chat model (customer name obfuscated). they want a quantized 4-bit variant that supports our chat templates + function/tool calling + structured json outputs. putting it here for prioritization and bring-up checklist.

liam: quick q — do we already have FP16 baseline perf + eval pack for this family? any regression numbers?

asha: we have an FP16 run on internal bench (latency + rouge/qa slices) but no 4-bit runs yet. i can spin 4-bit experiments but need a clear eval suite and gating criteria.

maya: context: enterprise customer, SLA target is p99 < 150ms for 64-token requests on Dedicated. also needs deterministic structured outputs for downstream parsers. i think this should be P0 for Dedicated onboarding. @liam @jonah :eyes:

jonah: agree P0 given SLA. immediate checklist from infra/ops + ml side:
- baseline FP16 perf + qual (existing)
- quant 4-bit speed/latency experiments on staging gpus
- eval suite: NLU intents, slot-filling, factual QA, hallucination checks
- prompt/format compatibility tests (tool calling + structured json)
- fallback policy (if quant fails, route to fp16 or smaller model)

liam: example chat template we should validate against (use for automated evals and client docs):
```
System: You are an assistant that answers using the "order" tool for commerce queries. Return VALID_JSON only when calling the tool.
User: {user_message}
Assistant: If you need to place an order, call order_tool with {\"item_id\": str, \"qty\": int}. Otherwise respond in one paragraph.
```
And a sample function signature for tool-calling tests: 
```json
{
  "name": "order_tool",
  "description": "Place an order",
  "parameters": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "item_id": {"type": "string"},
      "qty": {"type": "integer"}
    },
    "required": ["item_id","qty"]
  }
}
```

asha: quant experiment notes:
- run inference with same random seeds and sampling configs as FP16 to compare output diffs
- measure token-level divergence, intent accuracy, and structured-parse success rate
- run 3 seeds and take median to avoid fluke regressions
- collect perplexity + calibration shifts (temp sweep)

eva: gating proposal for go/no-go and rollout:
- structured-parse success >= 98% on core templates
- intent accuracy drop <= 1.5% absolute vs FP16 on our NLU suite
- latency p95 <= target (customer target + 10%)
- no new catastrophic hallucination patterns found in 2k adversarial prompts
- if any failure, auto-fallback to FP16 or smaller verified variant

maya: ops checklist before canary:
- prod config for model variants (quant/fp16) + routing policy ready
- monitoring dashboards (token cost, latency, parse-failure rate)
- canary plan: gradual traffic 1% -> 5% -> 20% with automatic rollback trigger on parse-failure + latency spikes

jonah: QA/automation tasks:
- add structured-output unit tests to repo (examples + negative cases)
- add quant vs fp16 nightly bench job for 2 weeks after rollout
- small synthetic workload that exercises tool-calls + nested json outputs

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline: model artifact uploaded to staging, container build queued (job #4482) :rocket:

maya: action items:
- asha: start 4-bit experiment (priority: perf + accuracy), share results in this thread by EOD+2
- liam: prepare chat templates + function signatures for eval harness
- jonah: draft canary + rollback triggers and update dashboards
- eva: finalize gating thresholds and sign-off with sales/security

maya: thanks team — keeping thread as intake + orchestration log. well convert accepted checklist into the onboarding runbook once gates are met. :white_check_mark:
